overview.h1: HTS Chapter 66: Umbrellas, Walking Sticks, Whips & Umbrella Parts — 2026 Tariff Rates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 66 Tariff Rates 2026: Umbrella, Walking Stick & Umbrella Frame Import Duty | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 8 HTS Chapter 66 lines: rain, golf, patio and beach umbrellas, walking sticks and canes, whips and riding crops, umbrella frames, handles and parts. General, FTA and Column 2 rates plus the 2026 extra duty by country.

overview.intro:
Chapter 66 covers **umbrellas and sun umbrellas** — rain, golf, folding and stick umbrellas, parasols and patio, beach and garden umbrellas — **walking sticks, canes, seat sticks, whips and riding crops**, and **umbrella frames, handles and other parts**. Its **8 tariff lines** run from Free (telescopic umbrellas, rain-umbrella frames, handles and tips) to 12% (other umbrella frames); patio umbrellas pay 6.5%, stick and golf umbrellas 8.2%, walking sticks 4%.

The extra duty by country decides the cost. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** on every line — **12.5% from China and Vietnam**, 10% from Cambodia, India and Indonesia — and no Chapter 66 line is on an exemption or exception list. China also pays **7.5% (List 4A)** on walking sticks and umbrella handles; its umbrellas are on no older China list. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada enter free, and EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total. U.S. imports were **$552M in 2025**, and **China supplied 89%**.

workedExamples.title: Folding umbrellas from China: telescopic vs. fixed shaft
workedExamples.body: A folding umbrella with a telescopic shaft is Free at the base rate; the 2026 Section 301 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.31), so a $10,000 shipment pays **$1,250**. Umbrellas are on no older China list (List 4B was suspended). A golf umbrella with a fixed shaft is 6601.99 at 8.2% (NY N347448): **$2,070** on the same shipment.

workedExamples.title: Patio umbrellas: Vietnam vs. Cambodia vs. Italy vs. Mexico
workedExamples.body: Patio, market and beach umbrellas are garden umbrellas at 6.5% (HQ H248132). From Vietnam: 6.5% + 12.5% = **$1,900** on $10,000. From Cambodia: 6.5% + 10% = **$1,650**. From Italy the EU rule replaces the base rate with 10% in total: **$1,000**. From Mexico with a USMCA claim: **$0**.

workedExamples.title: Walking canes from China, with and without 9817.00.96
workedExamples.body: Canes are 4%. From China, List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15) and the 2026 action (+12.5%) stack: **$2,400** on $10,000. Canes specially designed for people with chronic mobility impairments can be entered under 9817.00.96 (NY N356862, N352521): Free, and Chapter 98 entries pay no Section 301 duty, so **$0** when CBP accepts the claim.

workedExamples.title: Umbrella frames: rain umbrellas vs. patio umbrellas
workedExamples.body: Frames for patio and other umbrellas pay 12%; frames for hand-held rain umbrellas (6603.20.30) are Free. From China a $10,000 shipment of patio frames pays 12% + 12.5% = **$2,450**, rain-umbrella frames **$1,250**. From Taiwan the patio frames pay only their 12% base rate (**$1,200**), because the Taiwan rule charges nothing extra at 10% or more.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) measure walking-sticks or the like (heading 9017); (b) firearm-sticks, sword-sticks, loaded walking-sticks or the like (chapter 93); or (c) goods of chapter 95 (for example, toy umbrellas, toy sun umbrellas).

**Note 2.** Heading 6603 does not cover parts, trimmings or accessories of textile material, or covers, tassels, thongs, umbrella cases or the like, of any material. Such goods entered with, but not fitted to, articles of heading 6601 or 6602 are to be classified separately and are not to be treated as forming part of those articles.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 66 Tariff Updates: Umbrellas, Walking Sticks & Umbrella Parts (2025–2026)

seo.title: HTS Chapter 66 Tariff Updates 2026: Umbrellas & Walking Sticks — Section 301, China List 4A, IEEPA End | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 66 umbrellas, walking sticks, whips and umbrella parts since January 2025: unchanged base rates, the IEEPA tariffs and their end, the Section 122 surcharge, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, China's List 4A duty and the Section 232 aluminum listing of umbrella bases and other parts.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 8 Chapter 66 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA tariffs added 20%–30% on Chinese umbrellas (125% more for a month in April–May 2025), 19%–20% on umbrellas from Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia and Taiwan, and up to 50% on Indian goods. They **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%** on every Chapter 66 line — no exemption or exception list names one. China also keeps its **7.5% List 4A duty** on walking sticks and umbrella handles; Chinese umbrellas themselves were on List 4B, which never took effect.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 66 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 4A, the Section 232 aluminum duty on Russian aluminum derivatives (6603.90.81), the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA, Section 122 and Section 232 aluminum-derivative duties that have ended. No Chapter 66 line is on the Canada Section 338 lists (U.S. note 51), and no antidumping or countervailing duty order covers an umbrella, walking stick or umbrella part. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

stats.label: Extra duties in effect
stats.note: Section 301 (2026, Brazil, China List 4A) and Section 232 aluminum (Russia)

inEffect.exemption: Two Section 301 duties. The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) on all 8 lines. China List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15; 15% from September 1, 2019, cut to 7.5% from February 14, 2020) covers walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602.00.00) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41). Umbrellas (6601), umbrella frames (6603.20) and other parts (6603.90.81) were on List 4B, which USTR suspended in December 2019 before it took effect, so they are on no China list. No China exclusion covers a Chapter 66 product, and USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018–2019 actions continue. The IEEPA duties on China (20% fentanyl, 10% from November 10, 2025, plus 10% reciprocal) ended February 24, 2026; the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese umbrellas pay the base rate plus 12.5%: 12.5% on telescopic folding umbrellas, 19% on patio and beach umbrellas, 20.7% on golf and stick umbrellas. Walking sticks pay 24% and umbrella handles 20%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any note 52(j) country exception list. The 20% IEEPA reciprocal duty on Vietnam ended February 24, 2026; the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese umbrellas pay the base rate plus 12.5% — 12.5% on telescopic umbrellas, 19% on patio umbrellas, 20.7% on golf and stick umbrellas; walking sticks 16.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total (9903.05.76) when the base rate is lower; patio-umbrella frames (6603.20.90, 12%) pay their base rate only. Taiwan's exception list names no Chapter 66 line. The 20% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese umbrellas and walking sticks pay 10% of value in place of the base rate; patio-umbrella frames pay 12%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any note 52(j) country exception list. GSP has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026; the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Cambodian umbrellas pay the base rate plus 10% — 10% on telescopic umbrellas, 18.2% on stick umbrellas.

inEffect.exemption: For EU goods whose base rate is under 10%, the total is 10% (9903.05.39); at 10% or more no Section 301 duty is due (9903.05.38) — that covers patio-umbrella frames (6603.20.90, 12%). The EU exception list (note 52(j)) names no Chapter 66 line. This replaced the 15% IEEPA rate, which ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Italian and German umbrellas, walking sticks and parts pay 10% of value in place of the base rate; patio-umbrella frames pay their 12% base rate only.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods entered under USMCA pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94) and no base rate. Under General Note 11 an umbrella qualifies when made from materials of another heading, except when it combines both an imported frame (6603.20) and imported canopy fabric; walking sticks qualify from any other heading and parts from any other chapter. The 25% IEEPA duty on Mexico ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican umbrellas and walking sticks that qualify for USMCA pay $0; goods without a valid claim pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93) and no base rate; the same General Note 11 rules apply as for Mexico. No Chapter 66 line is on the Section 338 lists in U.S. note 51, so the 50% Canada duty does not reach this chapter. The 35% IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian umbrellas, walking sticks and parts pay $0 with a USMCA claim; without one, the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any note 52(j) country exception list. The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026; the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indonesian umbrellas pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any note 52(j) country exception list. GSP (SPI A, A*), printed on the dutiable lines, has been expired since December 31, 2020. The 25% reciprocal duty and the extra 25% on Indian goods (ended February 7, 2026) are gone. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian umbrellas and walking sticks pay the base rate plus 10% — 18.2% on stick umbrellas, 14% on walking sticks.

inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any note 52(j) country exception list. The UK pays +10% (9903.05.81) on top of the base rate. The 10% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British umbrellas pay the base rate plus 10% — 18.2% on stick umbrellas, 14% on walking sticks and riding crops.

inEffect.exemption: Japanese goods pay 12.5% in total (9903.05.49) when the base rate is lower — every Chapter 66 line. Japan's exception list names no Chapter 66 line. This replaced the 15% IEEPA rate, which ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Japanese umbrellas, walking sticks and parts pay 12.5% of value in place of the base rate.

inEffect.exemption: +25% under the Brazil action from July 22, 2026 (9903.05.01) and +12.5% under the 2026 action from July 24, 2026 (9903.05.27). No Chapter 66 line is on the note 50(a)(ii) Brazil exemption list. The 40% IEEPA duty on Brazil ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian umbrellas, walking sticks and parts pay the base rate plus 37.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Russia's goods take the column 2 rates (40% on umbrellas, 40% on walking sticks, 60% on umbrella frames, 45% on other parts) and the 2026 Section 301 duty (+12.5%, 9903.05.66). Other parts of 6603.90.81 — umbrella bases and the like — made with Russian aluminum also pay +200% under Section 232 (9903.85.68, note 19(k)), on the list since August 18, 2025.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian umbrella bases and other aluminum parts pay 45% + 12.5% + 200%; other Russian Chapter 66 goods pay the column 2 rate plus 12.5%.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (Thailand, the Philippines, Bangladesh, South Korea, Switzerland and others)
inEffect.now: +10% or +12.5% (10% or 12.5% in total for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan)
inEffect.exemption: No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)) or on any country exception list in note 52(j). Japan, South Korea and Switzerland pay 12.5% in total and Taiwan and the EU 10% in total when the base rate is lower. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Umbrellas from the other Section 301 economies pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%. Countries outside the 60 economies pay only the base rate.

changes.title: No Chapter 66 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 8 Chapter 66 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 4A continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018–2019 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 66 this keeps +7.5% (9903.88.15) on walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602.00.00) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41), on top of the 12.5% 2026 action.

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover every Chapter 66 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84): 12.5% for China, Vietnam, Thailand and the Philippines, 10% for Cambodia, India, Indonesia, the UK, Mexico and Canada. No Chapter 66 line is on the general exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) or on any country exception list in note 52(j). EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total and Japanese goods 12.5% in total; USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty; goods entered under a Chapter 98 provision such as 9817.00.96 (canes for the handicapped) do not pay it.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) on all 8 Chapter 66 lines; none is on the note 50(a)(ii) exemption list. From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added.

changes.title: Children's Product Certificates must be filed electronically with each entry
changes.detail: Importers of children's umbrellas and other CPSC-regulated products must file the certificate data electronically with CBP at entry (16 CFR part 1110). Goods entered from a foreign-trade zone follow from January 8, 2027.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum duty on umbrella parts ends (except Russia)
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the Section 232 aluminum and steel derivative headings with new 9903.82 headings and new product lists (U.S. note 16(c)). 6603.90.81 is not on them, so other umbrella parts no longer pay the 50% aluminum duty. The 200% duty on parts made with Russian aluminum (9903.85.68) still applies.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 66 line was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03), so every umbrella, walking stick and part paid it. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India ended
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) that had applied since August 27, 2025. India's 25% reciprocal duty continued until February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on all Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 66 line.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14357 lowered the IEEPA duty on products of China (9903.01.24) from 20% to 10%, so Chinese umbrellas paid 10% + 10% reciprocal on top of the base rate (walking sticks and umbrella handles also 7.5% List 4A). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) on top of the 25% reciprocal rate, for 50% in all on Indian umbrellas and walking sticks. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Umbrella bases and other parts added to the Section 232 aluminum list
changes.detail: Commerce added 407 product codes to the Section 232 steel and aluminum derivative lists, including 6603.90.81 (other umbrella parts and accessories, such as umbrella bases) on the aluminum list (9903.85.08, note 19(k)): 50% on the value of the aluminum content, and 200% for Russian aluminum (9903.85.68). The general duty ended April 6, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set each country's reciprocal rate: Vietnam and Taiwan +20%; Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines +19%; India +25%; EU and Japanese goods 15% in total. No Chapter 66 line was on the reciprocal-tariff exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025, so Chinese umbrellas paid 30% on top of the base rate (20% fentanyl + 10%). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%; other country rates paused
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% and paused the higher country rates for other countries, leaving the 10% baseline. With the 20% fentanyl duty, Chinese umbrellas paid 145% on top of the base rate until May 13, 2025 (152.5% on walking sticks and umbrella handles with List 4A).

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025 and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14228 raised the IEEPA duty on products of China from 10% to 20%. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01) from March 4, 2025; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10) from March 4, 2025, later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of China
changes.detail: +10% on all goods of China (9903.01.20) from February 4, 2025 — the first extra duty on Chinese umbrellas, which are on no Section 301 list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Lacey Act plant declaration now required for umbrellas and umbrella parts
changes.detail: APHIS Phase VII of the Lacey Act declaration schedule, which began December 1, 2024, covers umbrellas (6601), umbrella frames (6603.20) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41) that contain wood, bamboo or other plant material: importers file the genus, species, country of harvest, quantity and value (PPQ Form 505 or the ACE Lacey Act message set). Walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602) have been covered since April 1, 2010.

changes.title: China List 4A cut from 15% to 7.5%
changes.detail: Under the U.S.-China Phase One agreement USTR halved the List 4A duty (9903.88.15) on walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602.00.00) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41).

changes.title: China List 4B suspended — umbrellas never charged
changes.detail: USTR suspended the 15% List 4B duty (9903.88.16) that was to start December 15, 2019. List 4B named umbrellas (6601.10, 6601.91, 6601.99), umbrella frames (6603.20) and other umbrella parts (6603.90.81), so these Chinese goods pay no 2018–2019 Section 301 duty. Revision 21 still prints the list as suspended.

changes.title: China List 4A: 15% on walking sticks and umbrella handles
changes.detail: USTR's fourth China Section 301 list (9903.88.15) put 15% on walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602.00.00) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41) from September 1, 2019. Cut to 7.5% from February 14, 2020.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 66 goods fell from **$689M in 2024 to $552M in 2025** (−19.9%), the lowest since 2020 and well below the 2022 peak of $888M. **Umbrellas are 78% of the chapter** ($430M): garden, patio and beach umbrellas (6601.10, $270M, −17%), telescopic folding umbrellas (6601.91, $118M, −31%) and other umbrellas such as stick and golf umbrellas (6601.99, $42M). Umbrella parts were $76M — mostly handles, bases and other parts (6603.90, $62M) plus frames ($14M) — and walking sticks, canes, whips and riding crops $46M, the only group that grew (+2%).

**China supplies 89%** — $490M, down 23% from $639M — and $398M of it is umbrellas. The rest is small: Vietnam $15.6M (+53%, mostly umbrella parts), Taiwan $9.6M (mostly walking sticks and canes), Cambodia $9.0M (+90%, umbrellas), then Italy, Mexico and Canada at $3M–$4M each and Indonesia, Belgium and Germany at about $2M.

Through 2025 Chinese umbrellas, which are on no Section 301 list, paid the IEEPA duties — 20%–30% extra for most of the year and 145% from April 10 to May 13 — while Vietnam and Cambodia paid 19%–20% from August 7 and USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada paid nothing extra. Those duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Umbrellas, Walking Sticks & Umbrella Parts (HTS Ch. 66): Rules, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Umbrellas & Walking Canes: Classification, Lacey Act, FDA & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 66) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 66 line — Lacey Act declarations, APHIS treatment of wooden articles from China, FDA registration for medical canes, CPSC rules for children's umbrellas, origin marking — and the legal ways to pay less: telescopic and rain-umbrella classifications, 9817.00.96 for canes, USMCA, FTAs, rulings and drawback.
keywords: usda aphis lacey act walking sticks

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most umbrellas and walking sticks enter with only a customs entry, but four agency rules can apply: a **Lacey Act plant declaration** when the goods contain wood, bamboo or other plant material; **APHIS treatment and tagging** of wooden and bamboo articles from China; **FDA registration and listing** for canes sold for medical use; and **CPSC testing and an eFiled certificate** for umbrellas made for children.

The ways to pay less are mostly in the classification: a **telescopic-shaft** umbrella is Free where a fixed-shaft one pays 8.2%, **rain-umbrella frames** are Free where patio frames pay 12%, and **umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps** are Free where other parts pay 5.2%. **Canes for people with chronic mobility impairments** can enter Free under 9817.00.96, which also removes the Section 301 duty. Beyond that: claim **USMCA**, use **FTA** rates where the base rate is the cost, get a **binding ruling**, and claim **drawback** on re-exports.

levers.title: Classify by shaft, frame use and part type
levers.saves: The whole base rate: Free instead of 8.2% (telescopic vs. fixed-shaft umbrellas), Free instead of 12% (frames for hand-held rain umbrellas vs. other frames), Free instead of 5.2% (handles, knobs, tips and caps vs. other parts)
levers.document: Product specifications and photos showing the shaft construction, the umbrella the frame is for, and what each part is; a binding ruling if in doubt.
levers.caveat: The line must match the goods: a golf umbrella with a fixed shaft is 6601.99 at 8.2% (NY N347448), and beach, patio and garden umbrellas stay in 6601.10 at 6.5% whatever their pole (HQ H248132). The Section 301 duty still applies to the full value; from China, 6603.90.41 handles pay the 7.5% List 4A duty that 6603.90.81 parts do not.

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N347448 (golf umbrella, fixed shaft)
CBP ruling HQ H248132 (beach and outdoor umbrellas)

levers.title: Enter canes for people with chronic impairments under 9817.00.96
levers.saves: The 4% base rate, the 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty and, from China, the 7.5% List 4A duty
levers.appliesTo: Walking canes, quad canes and mobility canes for the blind of 6602.00.00 that are specially designed or adapted for persons with permanent or chronic impairments
levers.document: Product literature showing the medical design (weight-bearing handle, adjustable height, quad base); report 9817.00.96 with 6602.00.0000. A ruling such as NY N356862 or N352521 settles eligibility.
levers.caveat: Articles for acute or transient disability, fashion canes, hiking and trekking poles do not qualify (Chapter 98, subchapter XVII, U.S. note 4). Chapter 98 entries escape the Section 301 duties under U.S. notes 20 and 52(a) only when CBP agrees the claim is proper.

citations.label: CBP ruling NY N356862 (orthopedic walking cane)
HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on goods made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty plus the base rate (up to 12%)
levers.appliesTo: All 8 lines, for goods that qualify as originating under USMCA
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format. An umbrella qualifies when made from non-originating materials of another heading, unless it uses both an imported frame (6603.20) and imported canopy fabric; walking sticks qualify from any other heading and parts from any other chapter (General Note 11).
levers.caveat: Assembling an imported frame and imported fabric into an umbrella does not qualify. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Claim an FTA or AGOA rate where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate: 12% on patio-umbrella frames, 8.2% on stick and golf umbrellas, 6.5% on patio umbrellas, 5.2% on parts, 4% on walking sticks
levers.appliesTo: The 5 dutiable lines, for goods of Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman, Singapore, CAFTA-DR, CBERA and AGOA countries
levers.document: Proof of origin under the program and the SPI on the entry line (KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, JO, MA, BH, OM, SG, P, E or D).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)). GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding ruling before you import
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate: garden vs. other umbrellas, telescopic vs. fixed shafts, frames for rain umbrellas vs. other frames, umbrella bases (6603.90.81, NY N337801), canes (6602) vs. crutches (9021) and selfie sticks (9620)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where classification is in doubt — especially umbrellas with lights, fans or solar panels, and sets of umbrellas with covers or cases
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the product, its materials and construction (19 CFR part 177). Published rulings show how CBP decides: N337801 (umbrella base), H262581 (trekking poles in 6602), R02119 (riding crop), N298912 (selfie stick monopod).
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described. Covers and umbrella cases are not parts of heading 6603 (chapter note 2); they are classified on their own material.

citations.label: CBP ruling HQ H262581 (walking and trekking poles)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the goods are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported goods re-exported or used in exported goods
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods (for example frames and handles assembled into umbrellas for export)
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Lacey Act plant declaration (genus, species, country of harvest, quantity, value) for goods containing wood, bamboo or other plant material: walking sticks, whips and riding crops (6602) since April 1, 2010; umbrellas (6601), umbrella frames (6603.20) and umbrella handles, knobs, tips and caps (6603.90.41) since December 1, 2024. Goods with no plant content need no declaration

Walking sticks, canes and other articles of wood, twigs, vines or bamboo are wooden handicrafts inspected at the port of first arrival; from China, pieces over 1 cm in diameter must be treated and every package tagged with the manufacturer's identity

Canes intended for medical purposes (standard, forearm, quad and tripod canes) are Class I medical devices, exempt from 510(k); the foreign maker must register its establishment, list the device and name a U.S. agent

Umbrellas designed or intended primarily for children 12 or younger are children's products: lead limits for paint and coatings, third-party testing and a Children's Product Certificate, filed electronically with the entry from July 8, 2026 (toy umbrellas are chapter 95 goods)
Country-of-origin marking on each article (or its container when the article cannot be marked), in English, legible and permanent enough to reach the ultimate purchaser

Umbrellas of heading 6601 are textile products for origin purposes: a garden or telescopic umbrella (6601.10–6601.91) originates in the single country where it was wholly assembled, wherever the fabric or frame was made

citations.label: CBP ruling HQ 959701 (origin of garden umbrellas)

rules.title: Report the Chapter 99 headings with the line: the 2026 Section 301 heading for the country (or 9903.05.93/.94 for USMCA goods), China List 4A (9903.88.15) on 6602.00.00 and 6603.90.41, Brazil (9903.05.01), and Russian aluminum (9903.85.68) on 6603.90.81

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 19, 20, 50 and 52

groups.label: Umbrellas and sun umbrellas: rain, golf, folding, patio, beach and garden umbrellas
groups.note: Umbrellas with wooden or bamboo shafts or handles need a Lacey Act declaration (since December 1, 2024); umbrellas made for children need CPSC testing and an eFiled certificate.

groups.label: Walking sticks, canes, seat sticks, trekking poles, whips and riding crops
groups.note: Walking sticks, whips and riding crops of wood, bamboo or cane need a Lacey Act declaration (since 2010), and from China wooden ones must be treated and tagged. Medical canes are FDA Class I devices; they may enter Free under 9817.00.96.

groups.label: Umbrella frames, handles, knobs, tips, caps and other parts and accessories
groups.note: Wooden or bamboo frames, handles, knobs, tips and caps need a Lacey Act declaration (since December 1, 2024). Other parts (6603.90.81) made with Russian aluminum pay the 200% Section 232 duty.

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations — not legal advice. Lacey Act scope, APHIS treatment rules and FDA and CPSC requirements change; check them before each shipment.

keyTakeaways: Chapter 66 base rates run from Free (telescopic umbrellas, rain-umbrella frames, handles and tips) to 12% (other umbrella frames); patio umbrellas pay 6.5%, stick and golf umbrellas 8.2%, walking sticks 4%. None changed since January 2025.

Since July 24, 2026 every Chapter 66 line pays the Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — 12.5% from China and Vietnam, 10% from Cambodia, India and Indonesia — with no exemption or country exception list for this chapter.

China, 89% of the $552M of 2025 imports, also pays 7.5% (List 4A) on walking sticks and umbrella handles; Chinese umbrellas and frames are on no older China list because List 4B was suspended in 2019.

USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada enter free, EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total and Japanese 12.5%. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.

Canes for people with chronic mobility impairments can enter Free under 9817.00.96, without the Section 301 duty; wooden or bamboo goods need a Lacey Act declaration, and medical canes are FDA Class I devices.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 66 cover?
searchedAs: umbrellas, sun umbrellas, walking sticks, seatsticks, whips, riding-crops and parts thereof tariff
faqs.answer: Umbrellas and sun umbrellas (6601), walking sticks, seat sticks, whips and riding crops (6602), and umbrella frames, handles and other parts (6603) — 8 tariff lines in all. Measuring sticks (9017), sword-sticks (chapter 93), toy umbrellas (chapter 95) and textile umbrella covers and cases are classified elsewhere.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for an umbrella?
faqs.answer: Heading 6601. Garden, patio and beach umbrellas are 6601.10 (6.5%); other umbrellas with a telescopic shaft — most folding umbrellas — are 6601.91 (Free); other umbrellas, such as stick and golf umbrellas, are 6601.99 (8.2%). The country's extra duty comes on top: from China or Vietnam 12.5% more.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a patio, beach or sun umbrella?
faqs.answer: Patio, market, beach and garden umbrellas are garden or similar umbrellas, 6601.10 at 6.5% whatever their pole — 6601.91 and 6601.99 cover only other umbrellas (HQ H248132; NY N334613). A hand-held parasol is an ordinary umbrella in 6601.99 (NY N028017). From China a patio umbrella pays 19% in total, from Cambodia 16.5%, from Italy 10%.

faqs.question: Telescopic, folding or golf umbrella: 6601.91 or 6601.99?
faqs.answer: An umbrella whose shaft telescopes is 6601.91, Free at the base rate; one with a fixed shaft is 6601.99 at 8.2%. CBP put a fixed-shaft golf umbrella in 6601.99 although the importer claimed 6601.91 (NY N347448). From China the difference is 12.5% vs. 20.7% in total.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for umbrella frames, handles and parts?
faqs.answer: Umbrella frames are 6603.20 — Free for hand-held rain umbrellas (6603.20.30), 12% for patio and other umbrellas (6603.20.90). Handles, knobs, tips and caps are 6603.90.41 (Free); other parts and accessories 6603.90.81 (5.2%). From China, handles also pay the 7.5% List 4A duty: 20% in total.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for an umbrella base or stand?
faqs.answer: A base that holds a patio umbrella upright is an accessory of 6603.90.81, 5.2% — CBP ruled so for a fillable polyethylene base on wheels (NY N337801) and a beach-umbrella sand anchor (NY N281054). From China it pays 17.7% in total. It was on the Section 232 aluminum list from August 18, 2025 to April 6, 2026; now only Russian aluminum pays that duty.

faqs.question: How are umbrella covers, cases and canopy fabric classified?
searchedAs: protective cover for patio umbrella hs code
faqs.answer: Not as umbrella parts: chapter note 2 keeps textile parts, covers, tassels, thongs and umbrella cases of any material out of heading 6603. Imported with but not fitted to an umbrella, they are classified on their own — by material, usually in the textile chapters.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for walking sticks, canes and trekking poles?
faqs.answer: 6602.00.00, 4%: walking sticks, canes, seat sticks and hiking, Nordic-walking and trekking poles (HQ H262581; NY N197699). From China it pays 24% in total (12.5% + 7.5% List 4A), from Vietnam 16.5%, from Taiwan 10%. Replacement cane tips are 6603.90.81 (NY N353993); crutches are 9021.

faqs.question: Are medical walking canes duty-free?
faqs.answer: They can be. Canes specially designed for people with chronic mobility impairments — orthopedic, quad and mobility canes for the blind — qualify for 9817.00.96, Free (NY N356862, N352521), and Chapter 98 entries pay no Section 301 duty. Fashion canes and hiking poles do not qualify. Medical canes are also FDA Class I devices: the maker must register and list them.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for a riding crop or whip — and a selfie stick?
faqs.answer: Whips and riding crops share 6602.00.00 with walking sticks, 4% (NY R02119). A selfie stick is not a walking stick: CBP classified a monopod selfie stick in 9620.00.65 (NY N298912).

faqs.question: What is the import duty on umbrellas from China?
faqs.answer: The base rate plus 12.5% (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.31): 19% on patio umbrellas, 12.5% on telescopic umbrellas, 20.7% on stick and golf umbrellas. Umbrellas and frames are on no 2018–2019 China list (List 4B was suspended); walking sticks and umbrella handles also pay 7.5% (List 4A). The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What do umbrellas from Vietnam, Cambodia, Taiwan, Italy or Japan pay?
faqs.answer: Since July 24, 2026: Vietnam the base rate plus 12.5%, Cambodia and Indonesia plus 10%. Taiwan and EU countries such as Italy pay 10% in total and Japan 12.5% in total in place of the base rate (patio-umbrella frames at 12% pay only their base rate). Canada and Mexico pay nothing with a USMCA claim.

faqs.question: How many umbrellas does the U.S. import, and from where?
faqs.answer: $552M of Chapter 66 goods in 2025, down 19.9% from $689M in 2024. China supplied 89% ($490M), then Vietnam ($15.6M), Taiwan ($9.6M) and Cambodia ($9.0M). Garden and patio umbrellas were $270M and telescopic umbrellas $118M.

faqs.question: What else is needed to import umbrellas and walking sticks?
searchedAs: usda aphis lacey act walking sticks
faqs.answer: Goods with wood, bamboo or other plant material need a Lacey Act declaration — walking sticks since 2010, umbrellas, frames and handles since December 1, 2024. Wooden or bamboo walking sticks from China must be treated and tagged. Umbrellas made for children need CPSC testing and an eFiled certificate, and every article needs an origin marking.
